subject.title: fix(feishu): pace outbound sends per target

question: Should OpenClaw accept a Feishu-owned, default-off `sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs` config contract for proactive per-target outbound pacing?
rationale: Source inspection supports the missing capability, but the config name/default/override contract and acceptable proof bar for live Feishu send timing require maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Feishu Pacing
options.body: Proceed with this PR or a rebased replacement after real Feishu proof demonstrates same-target pacing and distinct-target independence.

options.title: Keep Only Reactive Retry
options.body: Reject the new config surface and document that OpenClaw relies on existing retry/backoff after Feishu rate-limit responses.

options.title: Move Scope To Broad Rate Limits
options.body: Defer Feishu-specific pacing and make the broader cross-provider rate-limit issue own queueing, budgets, and observability.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Feishu Pacing
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR or a rebased replacement after real Feishu proof demonstrates same-target pacing and distinct-target independence.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin metadata identifies this handle as the community-maintained owner candidate for Feishu-owned send behavior.
